{{Quote|Fuss fuss! Honestly, you screech more than a squirmy Ranat!|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], to [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]|<ref name="QOTE 2">''[[Queen of the Empire]]''</ref>}}
'''Ranats''', known as '''Con Queecon''' in their own [[Ranat (language)|language]], were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of meter-tall [[Rodent/Legends|rodents]] with long, tusk-like incisors jutting from their lower jaws. Though originally from [[Rydar II]], the Ranats there were nearly wiped out by [[Human/Legends|Human]] colonists in [[200 BBY/Legends|200 BBY]]. Three Ranats stowed away on a [[Spice/Legends|spice]] [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] and crash-landed on [[Aralia/Legends|Aralia]], where they re-established their species.

Ranat tribes lived in large, maze-like tunnel networks, where they raised their [[Youngling/Legends|young]] communally and lured intruders into dead ends to be [[Death/Legends|killed]]. Ranats had simple personalities, showing little evidence of emotion beyond the desire for food. Though almost always hostile toward one another, tribes did cooperate to kill pest-control teams after entrepreneurs arrived on Aralia to turn it into a [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] [[amusement park]]. The government of the [[Antemeridian sector/Legends|Antemeridian sector]] declared the Ranats [[Sentience/Legends|semi-sentient]], permitting sentient beings to kill the rodents in self-defense and forbidding them to arm members of the species. The [[Governor/Legends|governor]] restricted the movement of well-armed groups to Aralia to cover up the species' existence and its questionable level of sentience.

Few Ranats were seen away from Aralia, and those that left the world occupied the lowest levels of society. Ranats established themselves on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], where they lived in the more populated areas as scroungers and [[Merchant/Legends|traders]]. One group overran [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure's]] [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Palace]] after [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon|his death]], and the [[Vriichon brothers/Legends|Vriichon brothers]] once owned the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]]. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] military tested Ranat [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] bands for possible use against [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] forces. Ranats were also found in the employ of the mage [[Orloc]], who attempted to start his own [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]. The Ranat [[Rik-tak]] was a member of the [[Justice Action Network]] who operated in the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]].

Ranats were omnivores and strongly preferred meat, especially that of Aralia's native [[Roba/Legends|robas]]. Their sharp incisors and claws were useful as both weapons and tunneling tools. Burrowing wore down their teeth but also released hormones that stimulated tooth growth; unchecked, the incisors could reach prodigious lengths, so most Ranats gnawed constantly to keep them filed back.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Con Queecon, they call themselves. Big rodents native to the Aralia system. They're nasty&mdash;smart enough to fight but too stupid to understand surrender. It's illegal to arm a Ranat.|[[Sprig Cheever]]|<ref name="TFAD">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/fiction/f20050923/index.html|text=To Fight Another Day}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ranat_UAA.png|thumb|left|upright|Ranats had sharp incisors that grew from their lower jaws.]]
Ranats were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of small [[Rodent/Legends|rodents]].<ref name="GG4-1" /> They shared many features in common with [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species such as their distant cousins, the [[Tintinna/Legends|Tintinna]],<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> and with other sentient [[Mammal/Legends|mammals]]<ref name="AE">''[[Alien Encounters]]''</ref> of similar physiology,<ref name="GG4-1" /> including [[Chadra-Fan/Legends|Chadra-Fan]]<ref name="PIAFD:TTOMAK">"[[Play It Again, Figrin D'an: The Tale of Muftak and Kabe]]."</ref> and [[Squib/Legends|Squibs]].<ref name="TG 14">''[[Tatooine Ghost]]''</ref> Nevertheless, the status of Ranats as fully sentient or merely semi-sentient was the subject of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] debate for centuries.<ref name="GG4-2" />

With few exceptions,<ref name="NY CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Nevar Yalnal}}</ref> Ranats stood about a meter high. This small size made them seem innocuous to many who encountered them<ref name="CSWE III 77" /> and belied their power.<ref name="EGAS" /> They had short, well-muscled limbs<ref name="GG4-2" /> with four digits on each forepaw<ref name="EGAS" /> and three per hindpaw.<ref name="UAA" /> All four paws were nimble<ref name="GG4-2" /> and capable of fine manipulation. Ranats had short, heavy-duty,<ref name="UAA" /> retractable claws<ref name="NOTM">{{LivingForce|Jigsaw: In the Name of the Maker}}</ref> that, while of limited use in hunting or self-defense,<ref name="UAA" /> allowed a Ranat to dig through as much as one meter of soil and loose rock in a mere 15 seconds.<ref name="GG4-2" />

The Ranat body was tough, wiry, and partially flattened.<ref name="GG4-2" /> Exceptional flexibility allowed Ranats to squeeze through small openings that would prove impenetrable to other beings of similar size;<ref name="EGAS" /> the [[Shi'ido]] [[Changeling/Legends|shapeshifter]] [[Mammon Hoole]] often assumed the form of a Ranat to take advantage of this very ability.<ref name="GOF multi">''[[Galaxy of Fear: City of the Dead]]''; ''[[Galaxy of Fear: Planet Plague]]''; ''[[Galaxy of Fear: The Doomsday Ship]]''</ref> Although a typical Ranat had a long,<ref name="AGTTSWU-3">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Third Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> scaly, hairless tail,<ref name="GG4-2" /> the rodents were almost entirely covered in fur that ranged from dirty blond to dark [[red]]dish<ref name="EGAS" /> or grayish [[brown]].<ref name="KB" /> Some Ranats groomed themselves,<ref name="DA">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Diversity Alliance]]''.</ref> but for most, the coat was filthy<ref name="UAA" /> and foul-smelling.<ref name="EGAS" /> Understandably, many non-Ranats considered the species to be visually unappealing.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Ranats stooped when they stood<ref name="GG4-2" /> and scampered<ref name="KB" /> and scurried when they ran.<ref name="TW:TRT">"[[Trade Wins: The Ranat's Tale]]."</ref> They tended to wear little more clothing than cloth hoods, leather belts,<ref name="EGAS" /> and ornamental tooth bands.<ref name="UAA" /> However, those Ranats who integrated into galactic society often wore full-length tunics and footwear.<ref name="LOTE:CG">''[[Lords of the Expanse]]''</ref><ref name="NY CCG" />

The Ranats' [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], located at the sides of the head,<ref name="CRC 5">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> varied in color from beady and [[black]],<ref name="EGAS" /> to red.<ref name="NOTM" /> Their hairless, pink ears<ref name="EGAS" /> were small<ref name="GG4-1" /> and round<ref name="TFAD" /> and typically lay flat against the head.<ref name="GG4-1" /> A Ranat's long, pointed snout<ref name="TFAD" /> was full of sharp teeth<ref name="CSWE III 77" /> and terminated in a yellowish-white nose surrounded by long, black whiskers.<ref name="EGAS" /> Their senses were acute: they could see in the dark<ref name="UAA" /> and detect others' moods by scent.<ref name="TW:TRT" /> Ranats [[Ranat (language)|spoke]] in a voice of squeaks<ref name="BSMH:TBT">"[[Be Still My Heart: The Bartender's Tale]]."</ref> and screeches.<ref name="QOTE 2" />

A Ranat's bottom two incisors were sharp, pointed, and discolored yellow or brown from tartar and dirt. Gnawing stimulated glands in the Ranat's jaw to produce growth hormones. Unchecked, this caused the incisors to grow up to a centimeter in a standard hour. The only way to counter the growth was to gnaw even more and wear the teeth down.<ref name="GG4-2" /> Some members of the species managed to keep these teeth small enough to fit inside the mouth,<ref name="R CCG">{{CCG|set=A New Hope Limited|cardname=Reegesk}}</ref> but others had incisors that poked out and overlapped the upper lip like tusks.<ref name="GG4-2" /> Coupled with their sharp teeth and powerful jaws, these incisors gave Ranats a dangerous bite.<ref name="UAA" />

Ranats were fecund.<ref name="NJOSB">''[[The New Jedi Order Sourcebook]]''</ref> [[Gender/Legends|Females]] went into heat at least twice each standard year, during which period they mated with as many males as possible. After fertilization, the fetuses gestated for about 120 standard days. The mother then gave birth to a litter of three to six [[Youngling/Legends|young]].<ref name="EGAS" /> The species' signature incisors began to grow in at adolescence.<ref name="GG4-2" /> Members of the species were considered adults at three standard years of age, and the average Ranat could expect to live to be 20 standard years old.<ref name="EGAS" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Reegesk salutes Het Nkik and offers an exchange of tales or wares.|Reegesk|<ref name="TW:TRT" />}}
Although they were not intelligent by most metrics, Ranats were resourceful and crafty. They lacked the higher emotions associated with other species, consumed instead by the simple desires to eat and fight. This made them preeminent survivors and experts at scrounging, foraging, and getting into places that they did not belong.<ref name="GG4-2" /> However, it made them come off as belligerent, temperamental, self-centered, and stubborn to outsiders.<ref name="UAA" /> Notions of honor<ref name="POT">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref> and keeping one's word were only good as long as they did not interfere with the search for food.<ref name="UAA" /> Ranats insisted on their superiority to other lifeforms, calling themselves ''Con Queecon'' ("the conquerors") in their own [[Language/Legends|language]]&mdash;''Ranat'' was an appellation from others that referred to their rodent-like appearance. A few Ranats did develop more individual personality quirks, often coming off as paranoid. They gnawed incessantly to keep the growth of their incisors in check.<ref name="GG4-2" />

Ranat culture was otherwise uncomplicated.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Although Ranats used simple tools, such as rocks to stone intruders, they created no goods of their own, and only one Ranat in a hundred ever learned any advanced technological skills. Nevertheless, they readily adopted technology from without. They especially valued shiny knickknacks that they could hang from their clothing<ref name="GG4-2" /> or stash with their personal belongings.<ref name="UAA" /> Unlike most other sentient species, Ranats had no art, diplomacy, poetry, philosophy, or technology<ref name="GG4-1" /> and had a difficult time mastering complex devices or fields that required abstract reasoning. Nevertheless, relatively simple tasks were within their reach, such as firing a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]].<ref name="GG4-2" /> For example, Ranats enjoyed a game wherein they threw [[Chance cube/Legends|dice]] at one another and tried to snap them up in their jaws.<ref name="DA" /> Ranats familiar with the concept of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] were willing to work for little compensation.<ref name="SWE">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

===Diet and hunting===
[[File:Roba.jpg|thumb|right|Roba were a preferred prey for Ranats.]]
{{Quote|Who lives in Jabba's palace now?''"<br />"''It's vacant, except for the Ranats that scurry around chewing on the furniture and drapes.|[[Ken]] and Luke Skywalker|<ref name="ZTHR">''[[Zorba the Hutt's Revenge]]''</ref>}}
For Ranats, life revolved around obtaining food; all other impulses took a back seat. Ranats were omnivores capable of eating almost anything.<ref name="GG4-2" /> In fact, their concept of food encompassed everything from [[Carpet/Legends|carpets]] and tapestries<ref name="ZTHR" /> to sentient beings. They were particularly notorious for eating the young of species such as [[Human/Legends|Humans]].<ref name="CSWE III 77" /> They preferred meat to other foods and spent much of their time pursuing prey.<ref name="GG4-2" />

The species hunted in packs of at least five members. Their preferred prey were mammals, especially the [[Roba/Legends|roba]], a porcine behemoth native to [[Aralia/Legends|Aralia]]. Upon locating their quarry, Ranat hunters surrounded it and then went in for the [[Death/Legends|kill]]. One by one, the hunters ran up to their prey, bit it, and tore off pieces of flesh, retreating before the quarry had a chance to retaliate. Once the prey finally succumbed to its injuries, the hunters descended upon it, gorging themselves and carrying the remains back to the town to feed the rest of the tribe. The entire process was so efficient that soon after arriving on Aralia, the Ranats had depressed the populations of several game species.<ref name="GG4-2" />

===Combat and war===
{{Quote|There's nothing like a good fight.|Unidentified Ranat|<ref name="GG4-1" />}}
The only other drive for a Ranat aside from that of food was that of the fight.<ref name="GG4-1" /> Limited resources on Aralia, exacerbated by the Ranats' high fertility rate and overhunting, frequently placed Ranat tribes in conflict with one another.<ref name="GG4-2" /> Ranats showed loyalty to only their own tribe; members of other groups were always rivals and enemies. Nevertheless, by the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], some Ranat tribes showed signs of cooperation to oust offworlders from their [[Planet/Legends|planet]].<ref name="GG4-1" /> One favored tactic was to stalk a hunting party from a rival tribe. After the enemy had tired themselves out making a kill, their stalkers attacked.<ref name="GG4-2" />

Ranats were unflappable opponents<ref name="GG4-2" /> and unrepentant killers.<ref name="CSWE III 77" /> They preferred to fight with their sharp teeth, getting in a bite and then shaking their target furiously.<ref name="TFAD" /> Ranats who felt trapped by an enemy became even more savage as they tried to escape from a corner.<ref name="UAA" /> They had no concept of surrender; a fight lasted until one side had been wiped out or forced to flee.<ref name="GG4-2" /> If under blaster fire, for example, Ranats scattered and fled.<ref name="SSR">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref> Prisoners of war were killed and eaten.<ref name="GG4-2" />

Ranats held grudges. Any surviving Ranats from the losing side of a fight rallied their tribemates to mount a retaliatory strike known as a [[vengeance party]]. Preparations for such tit-for-tat offensives took on an air of festival, as the whole tribe prepared the warriors for their mission.<ref name="GG4-2" /> The concept of revenge was so compelling that some tribes hatched even suicidal schemes to get back at a rival.<ref name="TFAD" />

===Social structure and habitat===
[[File:Ranat.jpg|thumb|left|Ranats used their sharp teeth and claws to dig out burrows in which to live.]]
Ranats originally hailed from [[Rydar II]], but after being driven from that world, they adopted Aralia as their new [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. Aralia was a planet of tropical and semi-tropical climes.<ref name="CSWE I 39">{{CSWECite|I|39}}</ref><ref name="AGTTSWU-3">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Third Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> The Ranats' communities preferred the tropical forests found along the coasts of Aralia's landmasses, but the rodents could be found across the world. The species was divided into tribes of about 100 members.<ref name="GG4-2" />

These groups dug out and inhabited subterranean tunnel complexes known as towns,<ref name="GG4-2" /> [[City/Legends|cities]], or warrens.<ref name="NJOSB" /> These labyrinthine habitations had many levels that could sprawl to three square kilometers in area with more than 50&#32;km of tunnels. The convoluted passageways acted as a natural defensive mechanism, since intruders were unlikely to know the paths as well as their inhabitants. For additional safety, Ranat engineers dug out several dead ends in which interlopers might be trapped and killed. They also built several exits per warren and camouflaged them with branches, foliage, and twigs. The tunnels widened into large chambers in places, each of which was devoted to a single task, such as sleep, meals, storage, refuse disposal, or caring for the young.<ref name="GG4-2" />

Defective newborns were eaten,<ref name="NOTM" /> but healthy infants were placed in their tribe's nursery. There, the adult females took turns tending to and [[Breast/Legends|suckling]] them while the other mothers continued to fight and hunt. Accordingly, Ranats rarely knew the identity of their biological mother. These caretakers were rarely doting parents, and some were known to kill a particularly troublesome infant rather than put up with it. Once a young Ranat managed to grasp objects with both fore- and hindpaws, he or she began to venture out into the larger warren and onto the surface. Ranat children enjoyed roughhousing, although some youths were accidentally killed in such tussles. Still, the adults largely left them be.<ref name="GG4-2" />

===Language===
Ranats spoke a simple language named for them.<ref name="UAA" /><ref name="GG4-2" /> Spoken Ranat sounded like a string of short, high-pitched chitters and shrieks.<ref name="KB" /> Ranats squealed when in distress<ref name="GOTJ">''[[Galaxy of Fear: Ghost of the Jedi]]''</ref> or having fun<ref name="DA" /> and shrieked when in pain.<ref name="TFAD" /> Still, Ranat communication relied on non-verbal cues as well. Members of the species smiled to show contentment,<ref name="TW:TRT" /> blinked rapidly to show desperation,<ref name="MFMY">''[[Mission from Mount Yoda]]''</ref> and grabbed their tails to express intense fear.<ref name="ZTHR" /> The Ranat's whiskers twitched to express satisfaction and trembled to show happiness.<ref name="TW:TRT" /> Most Ranats could write their language.<ref name="UAA" />

Members of the species were capable of learning other languages,<ref name="GG4-2" /> including [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]]. Ranats tended to take simple names, such as Kleef, Marbor, Reegesk, Targan, and Veerz. Others, however, took two-part names, such as Engal Jeers, Nestra Pallik, and Nevar Yalnal.<ref name="UAA" /> While at least one Ranat, [[Nitram Con Queecon]], had a three-part name, "Con Queecon" was the name of his species.<ref name="NOTM" />

==History==
{{Quote|The Empire categorizes Ranats as semi-intelligent. It's legal to kill them in self-defense.''"<br />"''How lovely. I'll remember that if I'm attacked by one.|Sprig Cheever and Tinian I'att prepare to confront the Ranats of Silver Station|<ref name="TFAD" />}}
===Evolution and exodus===
The Ranats evolved on Rydar II,<ref name="CSWE III 117" /> a planet in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]' [[Rydar system/Legends|Rydar system]].<ref name="UAA" /> There, the species developed tool use, language, and complex social structures.<ref name="GG4-2" /> The world had been reached by outsiders by [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]], even falling nominally under the control of [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]] during the [[Jedi Civil War]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Sometime during the days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the Ranats were joined on Rydar by Human colonists. The rodent-like natives soon discovered that these strangers brought with them a delicious new source of food: their children. As the Ranats kidnapped and ate their fill of Human young, the settlers, who called themselves [[Rydarian]]s, grew increasingly agitated. In [[200 BBY/Legends|200 BBY]], the Ranats soon found themselves beset by an orchestrated campaign to wipe them from the face of Rydar II. The campaign very nearly succeeded in killing every last Ranat on the world.<ref name="EGAS" />

Only three Ranats survived&mdash;two males and one female, who had stowed away on a [[Spice/Legends|spice]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler's]] vessel.<ref name="CSWE I 39" /> The [[Starship/Legends|ship]] soon left Rydar II with the stowaways aboard and headed for the [[Aralia system/Legends|Andron system]], nearby<ref name="GG4-2" /><ref name="EGAS" /> in the same [[Sector/Legends|sector]].<ref name="TEAC">''[[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion]]''</ref> Before long, the Ranats ate the ship's crew, and the ship crash-landed on the Andron system planet of Aralia.<ref name="EGAS" /> There, the Ranats reproduced, eating any defective young and starting a new colony. Within a few decades, they had a thriving group<ref name="UAA" /> in the coastal jungles of the world.<ref name="GG4-2" />

The population eventually reached the millions.<ref name="EGAS" /> This pressured the Ranats to expand beyond the coastal forests. By the time of [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Ranats could be found from the prairies to the mountains,<ref name="CSWE I 39" /> even in colder climes that received regular snowfall. This population boom and the Ranats' natural inclinations toward hunting put undue pressure on Aralia's native fauna. As prey species became rarer and rarer, conflicts between rival tribes became inevitable.<ref name="GG4-2" />

===Amusement park boom===
{{Quote|Then I got an idea. If these smelly critters were formally declared, by an Imperial government official, to be only semi-sentient, they would have no claims to the land, and we could wipe them out using the most extreme measures available to us.|Excerpt from the journal of Hayzo Trebors|<ref name="EGAS" />}}
[[File:Ranat_fight.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Under Imperial law, Ranats could be killed in self-defense.]]
Despite their previous encounters with outsiders, Ranats remained largely unknown on the galactic stage. Eventually, new strangers arrived, the developers of an [[amusement park]], drawn by Aralia's location near the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]].<ref name="TEA" /> Ignorant of the rodent-like species' presence, the entrepreneurs began constructing a large facility.<ref name="GG4-2" /> Unbeknownst to the Ranats, the endeavor was headed by an entrepreneur named [[Hayzo Trebors]], who had obtained permission to build on Aralia from [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Targan]] of Rydar II,<ref name="EGAS" /> and from the government of [[Antemeridian sector/Legends|Antemeridian sector]].<ref name="GG4-2" /><ref name="TEAC" /> The park was called [[Project Aralia]].<ref name="CSWE I 39" />

At first, the Ranats ignored the newcomers, tunneling out their warrens as they had for centuries. The construction crews soon noticed when these warrens made their site unstable,<ref name="GG4-2" /> and the construction manager reported the problem to Trebors. The businessman hired pest control specialists, and the Ranats took notice: they responded to this affront by hunting down and killing their exterminators.<ref name="EGAS" />

News of the massacre spread, and, with it, news of the Ranats' intelligence. If the Ranats were deemed sentient, the project would have to show them to be "useless and undesirable" to obtain an Imperial permit to continue to kill them.<ref name="GG4-2" /> Nevertheless, Trebors took a different course. He argued to the Imperial government that the Ranats were only [[Sentience/Legends|semi-sentient]] and thus unprotected by such laws.<ref name="EGAS" /> For its part, the sector government feared that ruling the Ranats fully sentient and then still allowing them to be exterminated would not play well with environmentalists and high-ranking Imperial officials. They agreed with Trebors' assessment; the Ranats were heretofore labeled "semi-sentient."<ref name="GG4-2" /> Trebors' people, continually fighting the rodents off, managed to complete Project Aralia.<ref name="CSWE I 39" />

Word of the development's legal wranglings spread throughout the sector. By [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]],<ref name="TW:TRT" /> fearing the rodents might come to other planets, the sector government passed a law that forbade the selling of arms to a Ranat.<ref name="CSWE I 39" /> The government also took action to prevent armed groups from traveling to Aralia, ostensibly to protect the native ecosystem, but in reality to avoid further knowledge of the way the Ranats were treated from becoming more widely known.<ref name="GG4-2" />

After another amusement park, known as [[Galaxy Ways]], was completed, much of the world's landmass was given over to resorts. Aralia grew more and more popular as a tourist destination, famed for its unique rides and attractions, shops, and dining, all at affordable prices. The Ranats continued to expand with abandon, paying no heed to who officially owned each parcel of land.<ref name="GS">{{WEGCite|story=Trouble at Galaxy Ways|book=Star Wars Gamemaster Screen}}</ref>

Nevertheless, Ranat predations drove their forest prey extinct. Ranat tribes searched for a new food source, and they found one: Aralia's burgeoning tourist population. The problem got particularly bad at Galaxy Ways. The park's management hired exterminators, but just like with Project Aralia, the Ranats simply killed them. The owners eventually resorted to tracking Ranat populations under the park and, should an attack occur, quickly quarantining the area until it could be contained.<ref name="GS" />

During one particularly gruesome off-season, several Ranat tribes decided to raid Galaxy Ways simultaneously. They carefully planned the assault. First, they gnawed through the park's power supplies, leaving it dead and dark. Next, they disabled any starships on the premises, stranding their prey there. They knew they easily outnumbered the guests ten to one.<ref name="GS" />

{{RPG}}
Then they struck. They carried away any tourists they could find, leaving nothing but bloodied strips of clothing, tell-tale claw marks, and shrieks of horror to warn the rest of the park's guests. For their part, the park visitors had no weapons with which to defend themselves. Escaping their grisly fate became the order of the day.<ref name="GS" />
{{Endgame}}

===Galactic spread===
{{Quote|Ranats and Ryn. And the ship's captain is an ex-Imperial. I hate to say it, but it really isn't worth it. With supplies so low in the refugee camps, it won't take long for the Ranats to start abducting children for their dinner.|An unidentified pilot in a New Republic refugee caravan, on whether to send a rescue mission for a ship full of Ranats and Ryn|<ref name="NJOSB" />}}
[[File:Yalnal.jpg|thumb|left|Ranats spread to other planets, including Tatooine, where Nevar Yalnal worked as a spy and laborer.]]
Despite the government quarantine on Aralia, Ranats spread across the galaxy to worlds as far afield as [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="CSWE III 77" /> By [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], "son of a Ranat" had entered galactic parlance as a pejorative.<ref name="Sco">''[[Scoundrels]]''</ref> That same year,<ref name="TFAD" /> the Empire had taken an interest in the Ranats that went beyond Aralia's local troubles. Military scientists took Ranats from Aralia to investigate whether the rodents might be trained as weapons against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and then used as [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]].<ref name="GG4-2" /> The project proved a success, and the Empire fielded Ranat [[Spy/Legends|spies]], happy with the low wages expected by members of the species.<ref name="SWE" />

After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|defeat]] of the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]] and the subsequent rise of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the galactic government initially ignored the Imperial precedent and labeled Ranats as non-sentient animals. However, as evidence gathered that the species had language, the government reapplied the Imperial "semi-sentient" label.<ref name="UAA" /> The matter was appealed and remained under consideration for a time.<ref name="EGAS" /> On Aralia, at least for a time, the point was moot, as the planet became part of the contested [[Trans-Hydian/Legends|Trans-Hydian]] during the [[Thrawn campaign]] of [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]].<ref name="TEA" /> During the New Republic's rule, Mammon Hoole included an entry on the Ranats in his publication ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''.<ref name="EGAS" />

{{RPG}}
During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Ranats became one of the many species to flee the chaos. In [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], a group of them from [[Gyndine/Legends|Gyndine]] were placed with a group of [[Ryn/Legends|Ryn]] aboard a refugee vessel called the ''[[Wanderhome]]'', which joined the New Republic refugee convoy. Their ship's [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computer]] developed problems, however, and the ''Wanderhome'' failed to make a rendezvous at the [[Ralltiir system/Legends|Ralltiir system]]. [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]] convinced the captain of the convoy to send a rescue team, but most of the [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] were reluctant to risk themselves for members of two species that were generally disliked. Nevertheless, a group of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] eventually decided to follow through. They escorted the ship back to the convoy, sparing it from members of the Yuuzhan Vong&ndash;sympathizing [[Peace Brigade]].<ref name="NJOSB">''[[The New Jedi Order Sourcebook]]''</ref>
{{Endgame}}

Ranats were among the enslaved beings held aboard a Yuuzhan Vong [[Koros-Strohna|worldship]] orbiting the planet [[Myrkr/Legends|Myrkr]] in [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]]. [[Tenel Ka Djo]], [[Anakin Solo]], and other [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] formed a strike team and hit the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] to destroy a [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] lab.<ref name="SBS">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref> More than a century later, the planet Aralia was part of [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]].<ref name="TEA" />

==Ranats in the galaxy==
{{Quote|Calm down, little one. What did Wuher say?''"<br />"''He said he wanted no tipsy Ranats robbing his customers. Me, a Ranat! Muftak, can you talk to him? Please?|Kabe takes offense to being mistaken for a Ranat|<ref name="PIAFD:TTOMAK" />}}
[[File:Reegesk2.png|thumb|right|Reegesk lived on Tatooine and traded with the native Jawas.]]
Prior to their exodus from Rydar II, Ranats were uncommon in the greater galaxy;<ref name="NOTM" /> after their move to Aralia, they were still little-known.<ref name="GG4-2" /> Those who did manage to leave Rydar II faced intense discrimination in the galaxy at large. To beings who were unfamiliar with the species and their culture, Ranats were considered regular animals at best,<ref name="NOTM" /> pests or vermin at worst. Those who were familiar with Ranat behavior often reacted even more negatively toward them; the Ranats' taste for sentient flesh&mdash;particularly that of infants&mdash;placed them squarely in the company of the most hated beings in the galaxy.<ref name="GG4-2" /><ref name="BP">''[[The New Jedi Order: Balance Point]]''</ref>

The Imperial designation of "semi-sentient," which was brought back and persisted well into the New Republic period,<ref name="EGAS" /> meant that Ranats could not legally own property and had no recourse against being killed in self-defense. In reality, other sentient beings could kill Ranats without consequence,<ref name="GG4-2" /> as exemplified by [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan's]] use of Ranats in his medical experiments.<ref name="DD">"[[Doctor Death: The Tale of Dr. Evazan and Ponda Baba]]."</ref> For their part, very few Ranats were able to overcome the solipsistic behaviors that others found reprehensible in their species, and those who could found it hard to keep on good terms with non-Ranats.<ref name="UAA" />

Over time, the very name ''Ranat'' took on a pejorative tone, and other rodent-like sentients took umbrage to being mistaken for a member of the species.<ref name="PIAFD:TTOMAK" /> Being compared to a Ranat indicated an undesirable demeanor,<ref name="TPS">''[[The Paradise Snare]]''</ref> and calling someone a Ranat was a grave insult.<ref name="Recovery">''[[The New Jedi Order: Recovery]]''</ref> In 3 ABY, the [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Az-Iban]] flew a [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] called the ''[[Rampaging Ranat]]'',<ref name="SSR" /> a name that pointed out the species' reputation as mindless killers.<ref name="WWITMRB 45">{{InsiderCite|67|Who's Who in the Max Rebo Band}}</ref> Similarly, the [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]] smuggler [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]] owned a freighter named the ''[[Angry Ranat]]'' during the Galactic Civil War.<ref name="FF51">{{FactFile|51|CAN 11-14|Mos Eisley Cantina Characters}}</ref> In the early days of the New Republic, the musical group [[the Palpatones]] made light of anti-Ranat sentiment in their hit song "[[Kick the Ranat]]."<ref name="WWITMRB 45" /> To "not give a Ranat's whisker"<ref name="RB 21">{{GamerCite|6|Rebel Bass}}</ref> or a "Ranat's sneeze" were galactic curses.<ref name="POT" />

Still, some Ranats did manage to eke out a living in galactic society, often settling in large, populated areas.<ref name="CSWE III 77" /> A sizable number made their way from Aralia to the planets Gyndine<ref name="NJOSB" /> and Tatooine. On the latter, they attained some modicum of acceptance, taking on the role of scavengers and merchants. They were often compared to Tatooine's native [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]] and came into competition with them,<ref name="CSWE III 77" /> although the Ranats stayed mostly within the confines of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], while the Jawas roamed the deserts. Members of the two species traded with one another following a strict protocol. Still, people on Tatooine had little respect for the rodents, giving them the disparaging nickname "[[womp]]s," after the native [[Womp rat/Legends|womp rat]].<ref name="SM:TJT">"[[Swap Meet: The Jawa's Tale]]."</ref>

[[File:Rik-tak_and_Kelsek.png|thumb|left|120px|The [[Justice Action Network|JAN]] operative [[Rik-tak]] was allied with the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] recruiter [[Kelsek]].]]
One small tribe of Ranats inhabited [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] on Tatooine, where they had grown more accustomed to using technology than others of their kind. In 0 BBY, they were building themselves a [[Moisture vaporator/Legends|moisture vaporator]] and other items to ease their life on the desert world. Members of this tribe were present in the [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Mos Eisley Cantina]] in 0 BBY on the day [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] chartered the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].<ref name="BSMH:TBT" /> One of these was the thief and scavenger [[Reegesk/Legends|Reegesk]],<ref name="R CCG" /> who sat with a group of Jawas<ref name="ITWOSWT">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> and traded a [[Tusken battle talisman]] to the Jawa [[Het Nkik/Legends|Het Nkik]].<ref name="SM:TJT" /> Meanwhile, he palmed the [[Power cell/Legends|power pack]] from the Jawa's blaster to run his tribe's moisture vaporator.<ref name="SWFF CAN6">''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]''</ref> [[Nevar Yalnal/Legends|Nevar Yalnal]], an outcast from the other Ranats on Tatooine, lived as a spy and laborer in Mos Eisley. He took odd jobs spying for clients and doing manual labor for the [[Saurin/Legends|Saurin]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]] trader [[Hrchek Kal Fas/Legends|Hrchek Kal Fas]].<ref name="CSWE III 348">{{CSWECite|III|348}}</ref> The Ranat [[Vriichon brothers/Legends|Vriichon brothers]] owned the Mos Eisley Cantina, where they had set up an illegal [[Spice/Legends|spice]] den. They eventually sold the place to the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chalmun/Legends|Chalmun]], after which they made themselves scarce in fear of retribution should the corpses they had buried in the cantina basement be discovered.<ref name="ITWOSWT" />

Despite this relative acceptance on the planet, Ranats still met with prejudice; seven months ABY, Mammon Hoole and his charges encountered a Ranat being tortured in [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt's]] [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|desert palace]].<ref name="GOTJ" /> After the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord's]] death in 4 ABY, a group of Ranats overtook the abandoned palace. There, they ran about chewing on everything. Although Jabba's father, [[Zorba Desilijic Tiure|Zorba the Hutt]], reclaimed his son's property in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]],<ref name="ZTHR" /> memories of its Ranat infestation haunted his dreams.<ref name="MFMY" />

Nitram Con Queecon was a Ranat who lived in the ruins of [[Nub Saar]] on [[Genarius]]. He hated other beings and tried to scare them away with signs and traps. Nevertheless, in [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], a group known as the [[Heroes of Cularin]] arrived in the city and convinced Nitram to help them track down [[Togorian/Legends|Togorians]] hiding out nearby.<ref name="NOTM" /> [[Silver Station]] also had a colony of Ranats living on it. The Rebel Alliance operative [[Una Poot]] tried but failed to exterminate them when she arrived there. In retaliation, they threatened to blow the station up with [[JL-12-F]] explosives in 0 ABY. The arms heiress [[Tinian I'att Azur-Jamin|Tinian I'att]] disarmed their device and prevented their plan from coming to fruition.<ref name="TFAD" /><ref name="TPP:TTOB">"[[The Prize Pelt: The Tale of Bossk]]."</ref>

During the Galactic Civil War, the Empire abducted Ranats from Aralia<ref name="GG4-2" />&mdash;as well as other species deemed semi-sentient, such as [[aga]], [[Avogwi]], [[cidwen]], and [[Zelosian]]s<ref name="COTJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref>&mdash;and trained them as soldiers. The program was administered by [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] and [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] themselves, using drugs and mind control to mold their Ranat subjects into obedient guards.<ref name="CSWE I 39" /> The procedure began with the delivery of a hallucinogenic drug, such as [[brain-jagger]] or [[Black Hole (drug)|Black Hole]], to affect the Ranats' fear centers. The Emperor and his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] then used the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] to render the drugs' effects permanent. The fear-crazed Ranats came to be even more aggressive than normal, attacking any being who came within their range. The Ranats served in capacities where [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] were needed for other tasks, heeding the personal [[Telepathy/Legends|telepathic]] whims of the Emperor.<ref name="COTJ" /> The experiments continued even after the defeat of the Empire at the Battle of Endor. In [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], Ranats were among the beings undergoing intelligence enhancement in a program authorized by the warlord [[Zsinj]] aboard his [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]], the [[Iron Fist (Executor-class)|''Iron Fist'']].<ref name="XWSC">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref> The Ranats were later freed by [[Gara Petothel|Lara Notsil]] and helped her to escape the ship.<ref name="XWSC">''[[X-Wing: Solo Command]]''</ref> The Empire simply paid other Ranats to do their bidding; the beings were willing to work for very little compensation.<ref name="CSWE III 77" /> Around [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]], a female Ranat acting on Imperial orders approached [[Mechis III/Legends|Mechis III]] in a ship searching for rogue [[IG-88 assassin droid/Legends|IG-88 assassin droid]] models. When the droid [[3D-4X]] sent back doctored footage of [[Hekis Durumm Perdo Kolokk Baldikarr Thun]], the Ranat continued to the next system on its itinerary.<ref name="TIA:TTOI">"[[Therefore I Am: The Tale of IG-88]]."</ref>

Later, private interests, such as security companies, tried similar experiments.<ref name="GG4-2" /> In [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]], the self-proclaimed mage [[Orloc]] retained the services of a cadre of Ranat enforcers on [[Exis Station/Legends|Exis Station]]. He used a "voice of command" to order them to do his bidding, but in reality, this was only a technological gimmick. The Ranats salvaged components from the station's ruins when off-duty. They captured the Jedi trainee [[Uldir Lochett]] and delivered him to their master. When Lochett's companions from Luke Skywalker's [[Jedi Praxeum]] came to rescue him, the Ranats stood in their way but were defeated.<ref name="KB" />

A small number of extraordinary Ranats managed to adjust to galactic society and use galactic-standard technology. Some of these found work as [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]] and [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]]. Due to the preconceptions about their species being primitive and mindless, such Ranats often gained the advantage in combat due to their opponents' underestimation of their capabilities.<ref name="GG4-2" /> Others worked as [[Fringer/Legends|fringers]] or [[Scoundrel/Legends|scoundrels]]. No Ranat was ever known to be able to use [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="UAA" /> One member of the species served in the retinue of [[Decca Besadii Diori|Decca the Hutt]] on [[Mawan/Legends|Mawan]] in [[26 BBY/Legends|26 BBY]].<ref name="TST">''[[Jedi Quest: The Shadow Trap]]''</ref> Later, during the Galactic Civil War, the Ranat [[Rik-tak]] worked as an [[Air taxi/Legends|air taxi]] driver and [[Justice Action Network]] operative in the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]]; he defied stereotypes as an amiable and helpful guide to his clients, although he did listen for interesting chatter from his passengers so he could pass anything useful along to the JAN cell operating in Tapani.<ref name="LOTE:CG" /> The smuggler [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] encountered a well-groomed member of the species who was a patron at the [[Yarith Bespin/Legends|Yarith Bespin]] lounge in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]],<ref name="DA" /> while another Ranat served as an assistant to the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Information broker/Legends|information broker]] who operated from [[Shanko's Hive]] on [[Borgo Prime/Legends|Borgo Prime]] in [[23 ABY/Legends|23 ABY]] and [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]].<ref name="YJK multi">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Shadow Academy]]''; ''[[Diversity Alliance]];'' ''[[Young Jedi Knights: Delusions of Grandeur]]''.</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:ReegeskSketch-CantinaRollCall.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Artist John Mollo sketched a rodent-like alien for ''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope''. The mask was eliminated from the final design.]]
During production of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], first released in [[1977]], artist [[John Mollo]] included a rat-like alien among his costume sketches for the patrons of the film's cantina sequence. The production team dubbed the character "Rodent" and "Rat Face." Although Mollo's drawing gave the cloaked and hooded figure a [[Breath mask/Legends|breath mask]], the design team eliminated this detail in the final production. The character was later given the proper name Aceatta.<ref name="CRC" /> Someone wearing the rat-faced mask appears as a background extra in outdoor scenes set in Mos Eisley spaceport and in the Mos Eisley Cantina.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref><ref name="RG">{{InsiderCite|130|Rogues Gallery|Rogues Gallery: The Unusual Suspects: Who's Who in Mos Eisley}}</ref> The scenes were filmed as part of principal photography in [[Wikipedia:London|London]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]];<ref name="CRC">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> in at least the cantina scenes, the mask was worn by actress [[Sadie Edon|Sadie Eddon]]<ref name="SWC">''[[Star Wars Chronicles]]''</ref> and was featured more prominently in an early cut of the cantina sequence.<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> This character appears as an audience member in "[[The Emperor's Court]]," a non-[[canon]]ical story from ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'', first published in [[December]] [[2002]].

In [[1989]], [[Troy Denning]] included the rat-like Ranats in his book ''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]'', a supplement for the ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' from [[West End Games]]. The statistics for the species make Ranats comparable to other species in their agility but deficient in their alertness, intelligence, mechanical aptitude, strength, and technical aptitude. The game also makes Ranat characters work twice as hard as members of other species to learn technological skills. Still, the rodents receive a bonus to attacks using their sharp teeth.<ref name="GG4-2" /> The ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' from [[Wizards of the Coast]] also offers Ranats as a playable species. Its statistics give them a bonus to dexterity but penalties to intelligence and likeability. Ranat characters enjoy special abilities to bite in combat, see in the dark, and slip through small holes. Nevertheless, this version of the game also makes Ranats learn technology-based skills at a slower rate than other species.<ref name="UAA" />

In [[1995]] and [[1996]], [[Decipher]], established that two different rat-like aliens appear in ''A New Hope'' and identified them both as Ranats. Decipher named the one from the cantina Reegesk<ref name="R CCG " /> and the one from the streets Nevar Yalnal.<ref name="NY CCG" /> The cards' game mechanics reflect their Ranat namesakes. For example, the Reegesk card allows a player to "scavenge" through lost cards to recover devices, droids, and weapons.<ref name="R CCG" /> The Nevar Yalnal card, on the other hand, gives its player a chance to remove an opponent's spy from the game.<ref name="NY CCG" />

Ranats have since appeared in various roleplaying adventures, some of which offer multiple versions of the same scenario. For example, the adventure seed "[[Trouble at Galaxy Ways]]," published in the [[1992]] book the ''[[Star Wars Gamemaster Screen]]'', is designed to emulate a [[Wikipedia:Horror film|horror film]], with Ranats standing in for [[Wikipedia:Zombie|zombies]]. However, the book offers a lighter variant that has the Ranats searching not for sentient prey but for merchandise featuring the park's mascot, [[Ronnie the Rocketpack Rodent]]. The Ranats have become enamored of the plucky rodent and have even taken to worshipping him as a god. Accordingly, the only visitors who have to worry about being kidnapped, according to this variant, are those dressed in Rocketpack Rodent costumes.<ref name="GS" /> The later adventure "[[The Refugee Trail]]," published in the [[2002]] ''[[The New Jedi Order Sourcebook]]'', is designed to test the player characters' morality. If they opt not to mount a rescue mission to save a shipful of Ranats and Ryn, the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]&ndash;allied Peace Brigade takes them instead.<ref name="NJOSB" /> The [[2009]] article "[[Dining at Dex's]]" lists "[[Ranat's cheese soup]]" as a food item for sale at [[Dex's Diner/Legends|Dex's Diner]] on Coruscant. The article does not reveal whether this dish was simply named for the Ranat species or if it was an item of their own cuisine.<ref name="Dex 8">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/dexdiner/index.html|text=Dining at Dex's|int=Dining at Dex's}}</ref>

The book ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'' contradicts other sources with regard to the average Ranat lifespan. According to the book, Ranats entered adolescence at four or five, were considered adults at nine, and could expect to live to 55.<ref name="UAA" /> Several sources contradict this, so this article therefore assumes that ''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' is in error.<ref name="GG4 and EGAS">See [[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races|''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races,'' First Edition]], [[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races,'' Second Edition]], and [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>

Several rodent-like aliens of unidentified species appear in ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic books]]. For example, a [[:File:Possible Ranat from It Takes a Thief.png|hooded and cloaked rat-like figure]] is seen in a cantina on [[Diado]] in "[[It Takes a Thief]]," a story set in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. Similarly, the [[Krayn's bosun|bosun]] of the pirate [[Krayn]]'s ship in [[Star Wars: Jedi Quest (comic series)|''Jedi Quest'']] is rodent-like. Finally, a [[:File:Possible Ranat in Darth Maul 2.png|Ranat-like alien]] is pictured aboard a space station run by a [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] [[Vigo/Legends|Vigo]] in [[Darth Maul (2000) 2|''Darth Maul'' (2000) 2]], set in [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]]. However, without explicit species identifications, it is impossible to tell whether these characters are Ranats or members of other species, such as Squibs or Tintinna. The article "[[Action Figure Archive]]," in [[Star Wars Insider 75|''Star Wars Insider'' 75]], mislabels the Chadra-Fan character [[Kabe/Legends|Kabe]] as a Ranat, a misidentification the character suffered in-universe, as well.<ref name="PIAFD:TTOMAK" />
